summary: Cancelled prefetch ripple causing API-Gateway 5xx surge during high-priority tenant ramp
description:
Issue summary:

During a customer ClarionAI scheduled ramp (priority-weighted traffic), we observed a sustained increase in 5xx responses from the API gateway for ~18 minutes beginning 2026-03-13T15:22Z. The surge correlated with many prefetch cancellation events originating from the serving runtime and coincided with hedged-retry amplification from the ingress prioritizer.

Impact:
- ClarionAI experienced ~30% of their requests returning 5xx during the window; streaming sessions frequently reset and embeddings uploads saw increased first-byte timeouts.
- Affected customer SLA: Dedicated plan (ClarionAI).

Environment:
- prod | us-east | dedicated tenant: clarionai-prod
- Ingress stack: api-gateway v2.14, prioritizer v1.9, runtime-serving v3.2.1

Observed behavior and metrics:
- API-GW returned 502/503/504 spikes with error-rate peaking at 18% for that route.
- Accept queue depth grew from baseline 5 -> 480 during ramp.
- Runtime processes showed increased prefetch_cancel events and a small but measurable rise in ephemeral worker restarts (SIGTERM -> restart).
- KV cache lock contention saw >200ms median lock hold during the peak.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Simulate priority-weighted tenant ramp of streaming + embedding mix (mix matched to ClarionAI traffic).
2) Enable hedged retries configured with 30ms hedging window and aggressive prefetch cancellation.
3) Observe accept queue growth and prefetch cancellation logs on runtime nodes.

Logs / snapshots (representative):
- api-gateway/error_rate/15m: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/AG/errors?var=tenant=clarionai-prod&from=2026-03-13T15:00Z&to=2026-03-13T16:00Z
- runtime/prefetch/events: S3 logs: s3://redwood-logs/prefetch/2026-03-13/clarionai-prefetch.log.gz
- kvcache/lock-latency: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/KV/locks?from=2026-03-13T15:10Z&to=2026-03-13T15:40Z
comments: 2026-03-13T15:30Z - Support (Drew Kim): Customer reported elevated 5xx starting ~15:22Z. Provided initial graphs and asked for escalation to SRE.
2026-03-13T15:38Z - SRE (Aisha Patel): Observed accept queue growth and multiple prefetch_cancel entries. Tagging runtime and api-gateway owners. Collecting core dumps and runtime trace samples.

2026-03-13T15:50Z - Runtime Eng (Luca Romano): Early signal shows prefetch cancellation is leaving half-open streaming sockets and not releasing accept-queue slot promptly. Hypothesis: cancellation path races with connection reuse path.
2026-03-13T16:05Z - Support (Drew Kim): Customer applying temporary traffic-shed; requests status updates every 5m. ClarionAI confirms degradation impacting user-facing features.

2026-03-13T16:20Z - SRE (Aisha Patel): Applied mitigation - increased hedging window to 80ms and throttled prefetch cancellation for clarionai-prod tenant at the ingress. Error rate dropped to baseline within ~6 minutes.

2026-03-14T09:10Z - Product (Maya Singh): Requesting a follow-up patch to ensure prefetch cancellation always signals accept-queue release before connection handoff; proposed code owner: runtime-serving team.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Root cause appears to be a race between the runtime prefetch cancellation handler and the accept-queue release path when streaming sessions are hedged.
- Cancellation currently defers some cleanup to an async path which, under heavy priority-weighted ramp, accumulates half-open sockets and hold accept-queue slots longer than expected.
- Hedged retries amplified the surface area: short hedging windows (30ms) caused many near-simultaneous prefetch cancels when an upstream variant responded slowly, cascading into accept-queue growth and KV cache lock contention.
- No evidence of GPU OOMs or NVML resets; GPU utilization stable.
- Related behaviour noted: small uptick in ephemeral worker SIGTERM followed by quick restarts, likely from the ingress backpressure signaling a worker eviction when accept queue exceeds thresholds.
mitigation:
Workarounds applied during incident:
- Temporarily increased hedged-retry window for clarionai-prod to 80ms to reduce hedging amplification.
- Rate-limited prefetch cancellations for the tenant at ingress, allowing in-flight handoffs to complete.
- Added an edge rule to shed small-batch low-priority traffic earlier to relieve accept queue pressure.
- Customer resumed normal traffic after mitigation and reported restored success rates within 8 minutes.
resolution:
In progress - long-term fixes and next steps:
1) Runtime-serving hotspot: implement synchronous accept-queue release in prefetch cancel path to avoid deferred cleanup race (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4286). Target patch window: 2026-03-20.
2) Prioritizer: add safety cap for hedging concurrency per tenant to prevent amplification during ramps. Owner: ingress-prioritizer.
3) Observability: add a dedicated metric for prefetch_cancel -> accept_queue_release lag and alert when >100ms for >3 nodes.
4) Runbook update: add steps to temporarily widen hedging window and throttle prefetch cancels for affected tenants during ramps.

Follow-ups assigned to runtime-serving and ingress-prioritizer teams. Planned customer post-incident call with ClarionAI on 2026-03-17 to review mitigations and confirm patch timeline.
priority_follow_up_tasks: Implement synchronous accept-queue release in prefetch cancellation path (runtime-serving)
notes_for_customer: Apologies for the impact during your traffic ramp. We implemented temporary mitigations that reduced the error rate to baseline and have identified a fix in the runtime prefetch cancellation path. We will share the patch PR and timeline and schedule a post-incident review with your engineering team on 2026-03-17.
